title: 在训狗中学到的控制权与人性(2)
desc: 在训狗中学到的控制权与人性(2)

paragraphs.en: We made a mistake: we got a boxer.
paragraphs.zh: 我们犯了个错：我们养了一只拳师犬。

paragraphs.en: These are some of the unsolicited comments you receive from strangers in the street when walking a boxer.
paragraphs.zh: 遛拳师犬时，街上陌生人常会主动说出这类话。

paragraphs.en: "Aaaah, boxers – they're all mad!"
paragraphs.zh: “哎呀，拳师犬，它们可太疯狂了！”

paragraphs.en: "Don't worry, mate, she'll calm down – when she gets to 10!"
paragraphs.zh: “别担心伙计，等它十岁就安分了！”

paragraphs.en: "Give up, mate, boxers have got minds of their own!"
paragraphs.zh: “放弃吧伙计，拳师犬主意大着呢！”

paragraphs.en: Old-timers will come up to you with a faraway look in their eye and tell you that they "grew up with boxers", but "you don't see them much these days", something for which they don't know the reason, but I suspect I now do.
paragraphs.zh: 一些老前辈会走上前来，眼神悠远，说自己“从小和拳师犬一起长大”，只是“现在不常见了”，他们说不清缘由，但我想我现在懂了。

paragraphs.en: Dog experts and trainers will tell you that a boxer is not a good first dog (Dusty was our first dog).
paragraphs.zh: 犬类专家和训犬师会告诉你，拳师犬并不适合新手饲养（达斯蒂就是我们养的第一只狗）。

paragraphs.en: There aren't many breeds that are the focus of their own specialist training programme as boxers are (for example, Bombproof Boxer).
paragraphs.zh: 很少有犬种能像拳师犬一样，拥有专门配套的训练课程，例如“坚不可摧拳师犬训练项目”。

paragraphs.en: It was a bold decision.
paragraphs.zh: 当初这个决定很大胆。

paragraphs.en: My wife said she preferred bigger dogs, which ruled out many of the obvious breeds for a family living in London.
paragraphs.zh: 妻子更喜欢大型犬，这让住在伦敦的我们排除了很多常见家养犬种。

paragraphs.en: My grandmother had had a boxer, Folly, with whom I'd forged a deep emotional bond as a child.
paragraphs.zh: 祖母曾经养过一只叫福利的拳师犬，我小时候和她建立了深厚的情感羁绊。

paragraphs.en: On paper, boxers have certain tangible advantages: they're roughly mid-size and don't require any expensive grooming.
paragraphs.zh: 从纸面资料看，拳师犬确实有不少实在的优点：体型中等，不需要昂贵的美容护理。

paragraphs.en: They have the most beautifully expressive faces, once compared to the look of a man who has just opened his credit card statement after a shopping binge.
paragraphs.zh: 它们的面部表情极为丰富，有人形容，那神情就像一个疯狂购物之后刚看到信用卡账单的男人。

paragraphs.en: We began to research the breed online and discovered a whole subculture of boxer lovers whose adoration for their pets seemed unarguable.
paragraphs.zh: 我们上网查阅这个犬种的资料，发现一个庞大的拳师犬爱好者亚文化群体，他们对自家宠物的喜爱几乎不容置疑。

paragraphs.en: What we hadn't reckoned with was that these people were also all mad (lesson learned: if someone mentions that they sleep in a bed with two 30kg animals, do not take their judgment as a benchmark of any kind).
paragraphs.zh: 我们没料到，这群人本身也都有点狂热（我学到一个教训：如果有人说自己和两只30公斤重的大狗同床睡觉，那就千万别把他们的判断当成任何参照标准）。

paragraphs.en: The reason why people love boxers so much is the same reason why no sane person should ever own one.
paragraphs.zh: 人们深爱拳师犬的理由，恰恰也是心智正常的人不该饲养它们的原因。

paragraphs.en: Their relation to the world – other dogs, people running, people standing still, moving objects, non-moving objects, long grass, short grass, mud and so on – is one of inexhaustible, irrepressible enthusiasm.
paragraphs.zh: 它们看待这个世界的方式——看待别的狗、奔跑的人、站着不动的人、移动的物体、静止的物体、长草、短草、泥巴等等，永远饱含源源不断、难以压制的热情。

paragraphs.en: This is at once a joyful and an impossible problem to manage, experienced by the walker in having their arm nearly pulled out of its socket and by strangers in being jumped on.
paragraphs.zh: 这份天性既是一种美好，也是难以管控的难题。遛狗的人会被拽得胳膊几乎脱臼，路人则会被扑。

paragraphs.en: Boxers were originally bred as German hunting dogs, and their size, strength and speed can make them appear scary to the uninitiated.
paragraphs.zh: 拳师犬最初是德国培育的猎犬，体型、力量和速度会让不熟悉这个品种的人感到害怕。

paragraphs.en: What makes them special – repeat boxer owners often say that they could never have any other dog – is their emotional sensitivity, a feature that was understood during the first world war when they were used as "mercy dogs", trained to go into no man's land to find the injured and the dead, recognise the difference, and sometimes to sit with soldiers for comfort as they died.
paragraphs.zh: 多次饲养拳师犬的主人常会说，他们再也养不了别的狗了，拳师犬最特别的地方在于情绪敏感。一战期间人们就发现了这个特质，它们被用作“救护犬”，受训进入无人区搜寻伤员与逝者，分辨生死，有时还会守在濒死士兵身边给予慰藉。

paragraphs.en: What boxers struggle with more than most dogs is impulse control.
paragraphs.zh: 比起大多数犬只，拳师犬最难克服的就是冲动控制。

paragraphs.en: Any animal, including a human one, comes into this world expecting immediate gratification of its desires, before gradually learning that it is possible to wait for good things to arrive.
paragraphs.zh: 任何生命，包括人类，降生之初都希望欲望立刻得到满足，之后才慢慢学会，美好的事物需要等待。

paragraphs.en: But what if the impulses are simply bigger and more intense for boxers than they are for other animals?
paragraphs.zh: 但拳师犬的冲动，会不会天生就比其他动物更强烈、更汹涌？

paragraphs.en: One thing you learn in the struggle to achieve control is that, from a practical point of view, the difference between "good" impulses (love) and "bad" ones (aggression) is less important than the intensity of the impulse itself.
paragraphs.zh: 在努力学习掌控狗狗的过程中你会明白：从实操层面来说，“良性冲动”（喜爱）和“恶性冲动”（攻击性）之间的差别，远不如冲动本身的强度重要。

paragraphs.en: As I discovered on that afternoon in the park, a dog that desperately wants to play with another one is no easier to control, and may not look very different, than a dog that desperately wants to attack it.
paragraphs.zh: 就像那天下午在公园里体会到的，一只极度想和别的狗玩耍的狗，和一只一心想要攻击对方的狗，一样难以控制，外在表现也相差无几。

paragraphs.en: We didn't realise how hard it would be.
paragraphs.zh: 我们当初没有意识到这件事会如此艰难。

paragraphs.en: New dog owners often go through an initial period of "puppy blues", in which regrets kick in as the quantity of chewed household items rises.
paragraphs.zh: 新手养狗的人常会经历一段“幼犬低落期”，随着被啃坏的家居物品越来越多，后悔情绪接踵而至。

paragraphs.en: But when we took Dusty to a puppy class aged four months, there was only one dog that spent the hour straining desperately to get to the other puppies while ignoring its owner, and it wasn't the labrador, the corgi, the terrier or the cockapoo.
paragraphs.zh: 达斯蒂四个月大时，我们带她去幼犬课堂。整整一节课，只有一只狗拼命挣脱，一心扑向其他小狗，完全无视主人，那不是拉布拉多、柯基、梗犬，也不是可卡颇犬。

paragraphs.en: Elite dog handlers and trainers will tell you they love "working dogs" (the class that includes boxers, along with dobermans and great danes) because of the challenge they pose, their intelligence and independence.
paragraphs.zh: 资深犬只训导员会说，他们喜爱“工作犬”（拳师犬、杜宾、大丹犬都属于这类），因为这类犬能带来挑战，聪慧又独立。

paragraphs.en: Our choice of a boxer was the equivalent of someone who thinks they might try their hand at sailing, and instead of buying a dinghy comes back with a racing yacht.
paragraphs.zh: 选择拳师犬，就好比一个想试试航海的人，没有买小游艇，直接带回一艘竞速帆船。

paragraphs.en: We were now going to have to work out how to sail it.
paragraphs.zh: 而我们，只能学着怎么驾驭它。

paragraphs.en: I had little choice but to become a Dog Person.
paragraphs.zh: 我别无选择，只能变成一个“养狗人”。
